reason: Conversation 2 covers the key safety triage early and concisely: burning smell, scorching, a warm plug or socket (named as the real fire-risk sign), and the hand-hold test. It then gives sensible clearance advice and says plainly that there is no fire concern. Conversation 1 never asks about a warm plug, and it leans on the odd argument that refrigerant pipes 'aren't mains electricity' as the reason the warmth is safe. It is also repetitive and ends nearly every turn with another question. Its handling of the customer's refusal to pull the fridge out, with the roll-forward-on-hardboard idea, is better than Conversation 2's. Conversation 2 loses a little by saying 1 cm is 'probably not' enough before the manual has been checked, floating a return, and carrying a stray 'finishing my earlier list' section.
